note: v1 90.10 (seeds 0/11 90.10/90.08), first draft of POLYMETRIC TOOL TECHNO, 'where is the one', at 132 bpm. A PHANTOM BASS made only of harmonics 2-5 of E1 (no 41 Hz energy; the ear supplies the fundamental) plays a bar that is empty on the one and hits hardest on the and-of-2, so in the break, with the kick gone, the ear takes that hit as the downbeat and the kick's return flips the phrase by an eighth. Loops of 3, 5 and 7 sixteenths (909 rim, comb-filtered Em7 stab, open-hat accents) turn against the four-on-the-floor, realigning every 105 sixteenths; a sixteen-bar build doubles the hat rate every four bars under a Shepard riser so it seems to accelerate at a fixed tempo; the kick feeds a dark reverb rumble. Form: intro 16, A 32, break 16, B 32, build 16, peak 32, outro 16 (4:53).

v2 92.03 (seeds 0/11 92.03/91.97 vs v1 re-scored now that the album has more tracks 89.17/89.16): THE BARE OUTRO and a cleaner low end. The outro now strips to the kick, the rim and the phantom bass alone - the hats leave, so the track ends on the illusion it began with - and the sections breathe further apart (intro, break and build sit 8-10 dB under the grooves). The low end was 8-10 dB over the genre and swamping the overtones the phantom fundamental is made of: the phantom bass is down 4 dB, there is a 160 Hz dip, the stab's comb moved up to 330 Hz and a 900 Hz lift fills the thin mids. Spectrum 83 -> 93, cohesion with the album 64 -> 85, and the form reads as six sections on both seeds. (Moving the rim off the 3/16 cycle to a 9/16 one broke the form, 81.7; still to solve.)

v3 93.15 (seeds 0/11 93.15/93.12 vs v2 re-scored 92.71/92.69): polish, not a new layer (Harry's refine-and-polish note). THE HELD BREATH - pacing for the reveal: the intro now opens on the rim, the hats and the turning loops alone and the kick waits eight bars before it comes in, so nothing arrives too fast; and the last beat before each drop (into the second groove, into the peak) is silence, so the kick's return - the moment the real one is revealed after the break has made you hear the bass's and-of-2 as the downbeat - lands out of nothing. Also fixed a rounding bug that had dropped the peak's level point, so the peak sits at full level instead of creeping up from -2 dB.

v4 97.28 (seeds 0/11 97.28/97.33 vs v3 re-scored 93.17/93.13): THE RUMBLE KICK - sound design, not a new part. The four-on-the-floor was a 909 kick with an 808 sub tucked under it; now it is chirper-two's new machine-kit rumble kick (kr) on its own track: a real chest-hit with the deep-techno rumble swelling in after every hit, one circuit instead of two layers, and the bass and stabs pump against it. The low end is finally one instrument, and the swell between the kicks gives the groove a pulse of its own - compscore's rhythm term jumps 60 -> 91 and the spectrum sits within a few dB of the genre everywhere.

v5 97.31 (seeds 0/11 97.31/97.32, level with v4 97.30/97.34): NO CLIPPING, after Harry's 'some of our bass hits sound clipped'. chirp-eco's levels check found 15-sample flat tops and true peak over 0 dBTP: my master drove +8 dB into a hard limiter. Now the loudness comes from a fast third compressor (-6 dB, 4:1, 3 ms, +5 dB makeup) that rounds the rumble kick's hits instead of squaring them, a 14 kHz low-pass against inter-sample overs, and the song ceiling at -1 dB. tools/levels.py: flat tops 15 -> 5 samples, -11.6 LUFS, same score.
